advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle git-absent / unparseable-version in the floor preflight so it surfaces the same actionable UsageError diagnostic instead of a raw subprocess/parse traceback.
evidence: tests/conftest.py:54: `violation = _git_floor.floor_violation()` then `raise pytest.UsageError(violation)` — only handles the below-floor case, not git-missing/unparseable
ABSENCE: no try/except around the subprocess or parse in installed_git_version(); a git-absent or unparseable-version environment escapes the intended diagnostic path
advisory.finding: When `git` is absent from PATH entirely, `pytest_configure` -> `floor_violation()` -> `installed_git_version()` calls `subprocess.run(["git","--version"], check=True)`, which raises `FileNotFoundError` (or `CalledProcessError`), producing an uncaught internal traceback during collection instead of the clean, actionable `pytest.UsageError` diagnostic the change exists to provide.
advisory.suggested_fix: In floor_violation()/installed_git_version(), catch FileNotFoundError, CalledProcessError, and ValueError (from parse_git_version) and convert them into a floor-style diagnostic string so pytest_configure raises pytest.UsageError uniformly.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral test that runs the CI git-floor gate shell logic with a shimmed under-floor `git --version` and asserts it exits non-zero (and passes at/above floor), so the `sort -V` comparison is verified rather than only the comment string.
evidence: search for '2.38' in the workflow yields a single hit at line 292 inside a comment: '# tracker histories with `git merge-tree --write-tree`, a mode Git gained in 2.38.' — not in the gate logic
test_consumers_declare_the_same_floor (test_git_version_floor.py:248-253) asserts `f"{major}.{minor}" in text` for the workflow, which passes purely on the line-292 comment
ABSENCE: no test executes the bash gate's version comparison; a regression that inverts the `sort -V`/`head -n1` sense would leave all tests green
advisory.finding: The CI 'Git version floor gate' shell logic (the `sort -V | head -n1` comparison, `awk '{print $3}'` version extraction, and the missing-file branch) has no behavioral test. The two tests aimed at the workflow only assert string presence: test_ci_reads_the_floor_from_the_single_source greps for the floor filename, and test_consumers_declare_the_same_floor greps for '2.38' — which appears in the workflow ONLY as a prose comment (line 292), never in executable logic. An inverted or mis-extracted comparison that silently lets an under-floor runner pass the gate would not be caught by any test.
scenarios: A future edit swaps `head -n1` for `tail -n1`, or changes `awk '{print $3}'` to a wrong field, so under-floor runners pass the CI gate silently
The gate comment mentioning 2.38 is reworded/removed, breaking test_consumers_declare_the_same_floor even though the gate logic is correct — a change-detector on comment wording
advisory.suggested_fix: Extract the gate comparison into a small shell snippet (or reuse tests/_git_floor via a tiny script) and add a subprocess test invoking it with fabricated floor/have pairs — e.g. floor=2.38 have=2.37 must exit 1, have=2.38 must exit 0 — mirroring the existing PATH-shim end-to-end test for conftest.
